findings.title: Mixed string/symbol in fallback list causes duplicate locale file loads
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`. `SiteSetting.default_locale` is a String (from the model) and `:en` is a Symbol, so the array mixes types. `Array#uniq` compares with `eql?`/`hash`, and `:en.eql?("en")` is `false`, so `["en", :en, :en].uniq` returns `["en", :en]` instead of one element. The result is then iterated by `ensure_loaded!`, calling `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for both `"en"` and `:en`. Each call ends up in `translate_accelerator.rb#load_locale`, where `Regexp.new("\\.#{locale}\\.yml$")` matches the same `*.en.yml` file for both the String and the Symbol, so the file is loaded and parsed twice on the first request from an English (or default-English) user. Fix by coercing consistently, e.g. `[locale.to_sym, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, and storing/comparing `@loaded_locales` as Symbols in `translate_accelerator.rb`.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but never uses Hash storage
findings.body: `class FallbackLocaleList < Hash` only overrides `[]` and `ensure_loaded!`; no value is ever written to the underlying hash. This will silently drop any assignments made by `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` or callers that expect a real map (for example, an `I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...]` override in a plugin or future Rails internal). Either drop the `Hash` superclass and just respond to `[]`, or actually populate the hash so callers can read the configured chain (e.g. for diagnostics or plugin overrides).

findings.title: @loaded_locales ||= [] in ensure_loaded! is racy
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` does `@loaded_locales ||= []` outside of `LOAD_MUTEX`. Under MRI this is benign because of the GIL, but the assignment is not atomic and the subsequent `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` is also unsynchronized. The actual file loading is protected by `load_locale`'s mutex, so correctness is preserved, but the pre-check is misleading: two threads can both fall through to `load_locale` and serialize on the mutex for no reason, and a `reload!` interleaved between the `||=` and the include? check could change the meaning of the check. Move the include? and load inside the mutex, or accept the duplication explicitly with a comment.

findings.title: No test covers the new ensure_loaded! call in set_locale
findings.body: The added `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` introduces a custom fallback chain (user locale → site default → English) and triggers translation loading on every request, but no controller or initializer test is included. In particular there is no coverage for: (a) anonymous users falling back to `SiteSetting.default_locale`, (b) a logged-in user whose `effective_locale` differs from the site default, (c) the dedup behaviour between `SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`. The PR description ("Test 9") does not point at any spec either.

findings.title: PR description "Test 9" does not describe the change
findings.body: The PR body is just "Test 9" and there are no specs in the diff, so reviewers and future archeology cannot tell what behaviour was intended to be exercised. At minimum the description should enumerate which fallback chains and which anonymous/logged-in locale combinations are being validated, and link to the relevant spec files.
